links.title: UPSIDA PropertyHub — Available Plots
links.note: Plot-level land bank with indicative rates. No login.

detail.whatItGives: Individual plot records across UPSIDA industrial areas — the only public source with plot-level pricing.
detail.typicalUse: First stop when matching a project requirement to candidate parcels.
quirks: Paginated ASP.NET grid — no bulk export
GIS link opens OneMapUP with the plot pre-selected via UNIQUEPLOTID
Rates are indicative, not the allotment price
Desktop only in practice — the grid is unusable on a phone

links.title: OneMapUP — UPSIDA GIS Layer
links.note: State GIS viewer with the UPSIDA industrial land layer.

detail.whatItGives: Map-based view of UPSIDA plots and industrial area boundaries, deep-linkable from PropertyHub via plot ID.
detail.typicalUse: Visual confirmation of a plot's location and surroundings before a site visit.
quirks: Heavy map layer — slow on mobile data
Layer toggles are not obvious on first use

links.title: India Industrial Land Bank (DPIIT)
links.note: National GIS repository of industrial parks and available land across all states.

detail.owner: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Govt. of India (with Invest India, NCoG, BISAG-N)
detail.whatItGives: Cross-state view of ~4,500+ industrial parks, GIS mapping of clusters, and existing infrastructure — useful for benchmarking UP land against other states.
detail.typicalUse: Comparing UP's offer against other states for a multi-state site-selection process.
quirks: Formerly branded as part of the 'Industrial Information System' — now consolidated as India Industrial Land Bank (IILB); the NCOG-hosted iis.ncog.gov.in system is closely related, possibly overlapping data
Requires registration/login for deeper drill-down on some views
An automated check got a 403 — consistent with bot-blocking on a government WAF, not necessarily a dead link; confirm manually in a browser

links.title: Industrial Information System (NCOG)
links.note: NCOG's GIS-based industrial land and infrastructure information system.

detail.whatItGives: GIS layers for industrial clusters, external/internal infrastructure, and links out to state-level GIS portals and land banks.
detail.typicalUse: Infrastructure-layer detail (roads, utilities) around a candidate cluster, beyond what the plot-level portals show.
quirks: Closely related to India Industrial Land Bank — the two may be converging into one system; check both if one seems incomplete

links.title: YEIDA — Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority
links.note: Official YEIDA site — notices, schemes, and land allotment updates for the Yamuna Expressway belt.

detail.owner: YEIDA (est. 2001, UP Industrial Area Development Act 1976)
detail.whatItGives: Authority notices, residential/industrial scheme announcements, and administrative updates for districts along the Yamuna Expressway (Gautam Buddh Nagar, Bulandshahr, Aligarh, Hathras, Mathura, Agra).
detail.typicalUse: Checking current YEIDA scheme launches or notices before referring an investor there.
quirks: Several unofficial broker/aggregator sites use similar names (e.g. yamunaexpressway.co) — this is the authority's own domain, not a broker site; double-check the URL bar
An automated check got a 405 (method not allowed) — the site likely just rejects the check script's request type; confirm manually in a browser

links.title: GNIDA — Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority
links.note: Official GNIDA site — notices, schemes, and services for Greater Noida's industrial areas.

detail.whatItGives: Authority notices, scheme launches, and administrative services for Greater Noida industrial and institutional land.
detail.typicalUse: Checking current GNIDA allotment schemes or notices.
quirks: A second site, greaternoidaauthority.in, also brands itself as the official GNIDA site — the .up.gov.in domain here is the more authoritative government address

An automated check hit a redirect to an internal error page (frmHttpErrorPage.aspx) — consistent with this NIC-hosted ASP.NET site blocking non-browser requests rather than the site being down; confirm manually in a browser before treating as broken

links.title: Noida Authority
links.note: Noida Authority's official portal — notices, schemes, and citizen/industrial services.

detail.whatItGives: Authority notices, plot schemes, and services for Noida's industrial and institutional land.
detail.typicalUse: Checking current Noida industrial-plot scheme launches or notices.
quirks: Domain is not a .gov.in/.up.gov.in address — confidence on this being the sole official URL is medium; verify against Noida Authority's official social channels (@noida_authority) if in doubt

An automated check returned 404 on this exact URL — a sibling path (noidaauthorityonline.in/en) was also seen in search results; if this 404s for you too, try that path or search 'Noida Authority official website' fresh before relying on this entry

links.title: UPEIDA — UP Expressways Industrial Development Authority
links.note: Official UPEIDA site — industrial corridor land along UP's expressways (Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Ganga).

detail.owner: UPEIDA, Govt. of UP (UP Industrial Area Development Act 1976)
detail.whatItGives: Industrial land parcels and scheme notices along the Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Agra-Lucknow and Ganga Expressway corridors.
detail.typicalUse: Site selection for projects targeting the eastern/southern UP expressway corridors rather than the NCR belt.

links.title: Invest UP — Land Bank Page
links.note: Invest UP's own summary/entry point into the state's industrial land bank.

detail.whatItGives: A state-level overview and links into the IDA-wise land bank details (UPSIDA, YEIDA, GNIDA, etc.) — a good starting orientation page before going to a specific authority's own system.
detail.typicalUse: Framing the state's overall land availability for an investor pitch before drilling into a specific authority.

links.title: GIDA — Gorakhpur Industrial Development Authority
links.note: Industrial land and schemes for the Gorakhpur / eastern UP belt.

detail.owner: GIDA, Govt. of UP (constituted 30 Nov 1989 under the UP Industrial Area Development Act 1976)
detail.whatItGives: Authority notices, plot schemes, and administrative services across GIDA's development area in eastern UP — roughly 27,000 acres under its master plan.
detail.typicalUse: Site options for an investor targeting eastern UP / the Gorakhpur link-expressway belt rather than NCR or the western districts.
quirks: A separate ERP system runs at pms.gidaerp.in for project/works management — distinct from this public site; don't confuse the two
Not covered by UPSIDA's PropertyHub — GIDA plots do not appear in the UPSIDA plot-level land bank, so check here separately

links.title: BIDA — Bundelkhand Industrial Development Authority
links.note: Industrial land authority for the Bundelkhand region, headquartered at Jhansi.

detail.owner: BIDA, Govt. of UP (constituted under the UP Industrial Area Development Act 1976)
detail.whatItGives: Notices, scheme information, and authority detail for the planned integrated industrial and urban township in Bundelkhand — the region served by the Bundelkhand Expressway and the defence corridor node at Jhansi.
detail.typicalUse: Site options in Bundelkhand, particularly for defence-corridor-adjacent or lower-land-cost proposals.
quirks: The site is slow — the root URL repeatedly timed out at 25s in checks while inner pages (e.g. /about-bida) loaded fine; give it time rather than assuming it is down
Runs on a .co.in domain rather than .gov.in/.up.gov.in, which is unusual for a statutory authority — it is the address cited by public sources, but confirm in-browser before circulating it externally
Not covered by UPSIDA's PropertyHub — BIDA plots do not appear in the UPSIDA plot-level land bank

links.title: Nivesh Mitra 3.0 — Single Window Portal
links.note: UP's single-window system for investor approvals and clearances.

detail.owner: Department of Infrastructure & Industrial Development (IIDD), Govt. of UP
detail.whatItGives: Application tracking and department-wise clearance status for registered investors/units.
detail.typicalUse: Checking or progressing a specific unit's clearance status.
quirks: Requires registered login
Session times out quickly on shared connections

links.title: Nivesh Mitra — Know Your Approvals
links.note: Wizard tool that lists exactly which approvals a given business/industry needs.

detail.owner: Department of Infrastructure & Industrial Development (IIDD), Govt. of UP
detail.whatItGives: A guided checklist of required departmental clearances based on sector, scale, and location inputs — answers 'what do I even need to apply for' before touching Nivesh Mitra proper.
detail.typicalUse: First question from a new investor: 'what approvals will I need?' — run this before opening a full application.
quirks: Still hosted on the legacy niveshmitra.up.nic.in domain even though the main portal has moved to niveshmitra.up.gov.in — this may migrate; re-verify if it 404s

links.title: Nivesh Sarathi — Investor CRM & Grievance Portal
links.note: Invest UP's CRM for investment intents, land facilitation requests, and grievance redressal.

detail.whatItGives: One place for investors to log investment intent, request land facilitation, raise a query against any department, and track resolution — distinct from Nivesh Mitra, which is for formal statutory clearances.
detail.typicalUse: Escalating a stuck investor query, or logging a new investment intent/land requirement for facilitation.
quirks: Launched Nov 2022 — newer and less well-known than Nivesh Mitra; don't confuse the two by name

links.title: UPSIDA OBPAS — Online Building Plan Approval System
links.note: Online submission and approval of building plans within UPSIDA industrial areas.

detail.whatItGives: End-to-end online building-plan submission, scrutiny, and approval workflow for allottees, architects, and UPSIDA officers.
detail.typicalUse: Guiding an allottee through building-plan approval, or checking where a submitted plan stands.
quirks: Separate logins/roles for allottee, architect, and officer — point the right party to the right role

links.title: UPSIDA — E-Auction Notices
links.note: Live and upcoming plot e-auction notices, organised by region.

detail.whatItGives: Region-wise (Agra, Aligarh, Ayodhya, Bareilly, Ghaziabad, and more) listing of plots currently or soon up for e-auction, with notice PDFs.
detail.typicalUse: Time-sensitive — checking whether a specific district has an active auction an investor could bid in.

links.title: UP Industrial Investment & Employment Promotion Policy 2022
links.note: Flagship state industrial incentive policy — capital subsidy, SGST reimbursement, or PLI top-up.

detail.owner: IIDD, Govt. of UP — Invest UP is the nodal implementation agency
detail.whatItGives: Full incentive structure: a one-time choice between capital subsidy, net SGST reimbursement, or a PLI top-up, plus stamp duty exemption and sector-specific provisions, across Large/Mega/Super Mega/Ultra Mega investment slabs.
detail.typicalUse: Quoting exact incentive slabs and eligibility to an investor by sector and investment size.
quirks: Cabinet approval reported 3 Nov 2022; the published document itself is dated 4 Nov 2022 — cite the document date
invest.up.gov.in has intermittently presented an invalid/self-signed TLS certificate in automated checks — verify manually in-browser if a script flags it

links.title: UP Multi-Modal Logistics Park Policy 2024
links.note: Incentive framework for large private multi-modal logistics park investments.

detail.whatItGives: Incentives for MMLP projects with minimum ₹1,000 crore investment: 30% upfront land-cost subsidy on IDA-allocated land, 100% stamp duty exemption on leased land, and related provisions.
detail.typicalUse: Pitching logistics-park incentives to a large investor (₹1,000cr+ threshold).
quirks: Direct policy PDF not confirmed during this research pass — this links to the official Invest UP landing page, which links onward to the document; verify and update to a direct PDF URL when confirmed
Cabinet approval and GO both dated December 2024 — landing page carries the fuller detail

links.title: UP Unified Building Regulations for Industrial Development Authorities, 2026 (Draft)
links.note: Draft regulation to standardise construction norms across all UP IDAs — still in public consultation.
links.issuingAuthority: Govt. of UP (proposed — covers Noida, GNIDA, YEIDA, UPSIDA, UPEIDA, GIDA, BIDA)

detail.whatItGives: Proposed unified FAR/construction norms intended to replace authority-by-authority variation across Noida, Greater Noida, YEIDA, UPSIDA, UPEIDA, GIDA (Gorakhpur) and BIDA (Bundelkhand).
detail.typicalUse: Understanding where building norms are headed — NOT yet the operative rule; the 2018 UPSIDA regulations (and its 2024 update) still govern today.
quirks: STILL A DRAFT as of this research pass — released for public consultation; not yet notified/adopted. Do not cite as final without checking current status first
Confirms BIDA (Bundelkhand) and GIDA (Gorakhpur) exist as separate IDAs beyond UPSIDA/YEIDA/GNIDA/Noida/UPEIDA — worth adding their own portals in a future update

links.title: UPSIDA Land Development & Building Regulations, 2018
links.note: Base construction/land-development rulebook for UPSIDA industrial areas.

detail.whatItGives: FAR, setbacks, coverage, and building-approval norms for construction on UPSIDA-allotted plots.
detail.typicalUse: Confirming buildable FAR/coverage on a specific plot before an investor commits.
quirks: publishedDate left blank deliberately — only the regulation year (2018) is confirmed, not a specific gazette/notification date; do not infer one, source it from the document if it's needed

A substantially revised 2024 edition exists (see related amendment entry) — the 2018 base document may be significantly superseded, not just lightly amended; confirm current operative version with UPSIDA before relying on specific clause numbers

Served from eservices.onlineupsida.com, which is reliable. The same document also sits on upsida.obpas.up.gov.in, but that host times out intermittently — if someone sends you an OBPAS link for this and it hangs, use this copy instead
A copy also circulates on stagingupsida.com — a staging domain, not production; do not cite it

links.title: UPSIDA Land Development & Building Regulations — 2024 Update
links.note: 2024 revision of the UPSIDA building/land-development regulations.

detail.whatItGives: Updated construction/FAR norms superseding parts of the 2018 regulation — exact scope of changes not itemised during this research pass.
detail.typicalUse: Always check this before the 2018 base document for any plot-level construction question.
quirks: Hosted on upsida.in — a third UPSIDA-related domain alongside onlineupsida.com and upsida.obpas.up.gov.in; UPSIDA's domain sprawl is a recurring issue, confirm which is live if a link breaks
Title suggests a full revision rather than a narrow amendment — read it as the current governing document, with 2018 as historical baseline

links.title: UP Private Business Park Development Scheme 2025
links.note: Scheme enabling private developers/REITs to build commercial 'business park' campuses.

detail.whatItGives: Framework letting private developers, REITs, and global enterprises co-develop commercial/IT business-park campuses in UP.
detail.typicalUse: Pitching to a developer or REIT interested in building (not just occupying) commercial space in UP.
quirks: Naming is inconsistent across sources: the scheme is commonly referred to as '2025', but the file path itself says 'Feb2026' and was uploaded to the server in April 2026 — publishedDate left blank until the actual GO date is confirmed from the document text itself, not a filename

links.title: Plug-and-Play Industrial Shed Policy (DBFOT Model)
links.note: Ready-built rentable industrial sheds for MSMEs, via a DBFOT PPP model.

detail.whatItGives: Lets MSMEs rent-and-operate ready-built sheds with utilities already in place, instead of buying land and building — land stays with the IDA throughout the concession.
detail.typicalUse: Steering a smaller/MSME investor away from a full land purchase toward a faster, lower-capex shed rental.
quirks: Direct policy PDF not confirmed during this research pass — landing page only; source the actual GO/policy document on next review

links.title: UP Data Centre Policy 2026
links.note: Current data centre policy — replaces the 2021 policy, targets AI-ready and green capacity.

detail.owner: Govt. of UP — IT & Electronics Department, with Invest UP as facilitation agency
detail.whatItGives: The incentive framework for data centre investment: capital and interest subsidies, land, stamp duty and electricity concessions, plus specific incentives for Tier-3/Tier-4 facilities, an AI Compute Booster, and green/sustainable operations.
detail.typicalUse: Quoting data centre incentives and eligibility to a hyperscale, colocation, or AI-infrastructure investor.
quirks: The filenames on the Invest UP page are inverted relative to their labels — the 3.6 MB file at the '...UPDCP-2026-Notification-English.pdf' path is the FULL POLICY (linked here), while the 737 KB file at the '...2026/08/policy_En.pdf' path is actually the approval/notification. Do not assume the path name tells you which document you are opening.
Cabinet approval was reported 6 Jul 2026; the policy document itself carries 9 Jul 2026 — the document date is used here
Supersedes the UP Data Centre Policy 2021, which expired 27 Jan 2026 — make sure an investor is not still quoting 2021 terms

links.title: UP Global Capability Centres (GCC) Policy 2024
links.note: Incentive framework for global in-house/capability centres, aimed at tier-2 and tier-3 cities.

detail.owner: Govt. of UP — Invest UP as nodal agency
detail.whatItGives: Fiscal incentives and regulatory support for MNCs and Indian companies setting up Global Capability Centres (IT, R&D, finance, HR and back-office operations), with an explicit push toward tier-2 and tier-3 cities rather than only NCR.
detail.typicalUse: Pitching a multinational considering a captive/GIC operation in UP, especially outside the Noida belt.
quirks: Named '2024' but only notified 7 May 2025 — and the PDF linked here was re-uploaded to a 2026/04 path (20 Apr 2026). An earlier 05 Jun 2025 copy also still exists at a 2025/06 path. Expect this URL to move again; the '2024' in the title is the policy name, not its notification date.
A separate draft (Draft-UP-GCC_280924.pdf) is still indexed by search engines — do not cite the draft as the operative policy
The operative processing document is the Implementation Rules 2025 (nested below), not this policy alone

links.title: GCC Policy — Implementation Rules 2025
links.note: The operative procedure/SOP for actually processing GCC policy claims.

detail.whatItGives: The implementation rules and standard operating procedure under the GCC Policy 2024 — eligibility tests, application route, documentation, and sanction process. This is what a claim is actually assessed against.
detail.typicalUse: Working an actual GCC incentive application, as opposed to pitching the headline policy.
quirks: Nested here under the GCC Policy for convenience — it is implementation rules, not a formal amendment to the policy text
A Hindi version dated 07 Jan 2026 also exists at a separate 2026/01 path; this entry links the English rules dated 14 Mar 2026

links.title: PM Gati Shakti — National Master Plan
links.note: National multi-modal infrastructure GIS platform spanning all central ministries.

detail.owner: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Govt. of India
detail.whatItGives: Layered GIS view of existing and planned infrastructure (road, rail, ports, power, etc.) across India, used for infrastructure gap analysis around a candidate site.
detail.typicalUse: Checking planned connectivity infrastructure near a site, beyond what's already built.
quirks: The bare pmgatishakti.gov.in root 404s in automated checks — this /pmgatishakti/login path is the real entry point
Full layer access requires a login/registration tied to a ministry or state department

links.title: DPIIT — Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
links.note: Central department behind national industrial policy, EoDB rankings, and land bank tools.

detail.owner: Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Govt. of India
detail.whatItGives: National industrial policy documents, state EoDB ranking methodology, and links to DPIIT-run tools like India Industrial Land Bank.
detail.typicalUse: Referencing national policy or EoDB ranking context in a state pitch.

links.title: MoRTH — Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
links.note: National road/highway policy and project information.

detail.whatItGives: National highway policy, standards, and project-level information relevant to connectivity around industrial sites.
detail.typicalUse: Checking national highway policy or a specific NH project status.

links.title: NHAI — National Highways Authority of India
links.note: Highway project execution — status of specific NH/expressway stretches.

detail.whatItGives: Project-level status for national highways and expressways, including stretches feeding UP's industrial corridors.
detail.typicalUse: Verifying the completion status of a highway segment relevant to a site's connectivity.

links.title: NICDC — National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation
links.note: Implements India's industrial corridor programme, including nodes touching UP.

detail.whatItGives: Master-planned industrial corridor/smart-city node information, including any UP-touching corridor nodes.
detail.typicalUse: Referencing national industrial-corridor context alongside UPEIDA's expressway corridors.

links.title: DFCCIL — Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India
links.note: Rail freight corridor project status — relevant to logistics/MMLP site selection.

detail.owner: Ministry of Railways, Govt. of India
detail.whatItGives: Status of the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors, including UP-touching sections relevant to logistics park siting.
detail.typicalUse: Checking freight-corridor connectivity for a logistics or MMLP-policy pitch.

links.title: MoHUA — Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
links.note: National urban development policy and scheme information.

detail.whatItGives: National urban planning, housing, and municipal-infrastructure policy relevant to urban industrial siting.
detail.typicalUse: Referencing national urban-policy schemes alongside a state industrial pitch.

links.title: CGWA — Central Ground Water Authority (NOC)
links.note: NOC authority for groundwater extraction — needed for many industrial units.

detail.owner: Ministry of Jal Shakti, Govt. of India
detail.whatItGives: The No Objection Certificate process for groundwater/tube-well extraction that industrial units routinely need alongside state clearances.
detail.typicalUse: Pointing an investor to the groundwater NOC process when their project needs a borewell/tube well.
quirks: Domain confidence is medium — CGWA sits under the renamed Ministry of Jal Shakli/Dept. of Water Resources and may have migrated its portal; verify this URL still resolves to the current NOC system on next review

links.title: SEIAA UP — Environmental Clearance (via PARIVESH)
links.note: UP's State Environment Impact Assessment Authority has no standalone portal — apply via the national PARIVESH system.

detail.owner: SEIAA Uttar Pradesh (Secretariat: Directorate of Environment, Govt. of UP) — processed via national MoEFCC system
detail.whatItGives: Environmental clearance application, tracking, and committee-agenda documents for projects requiring EIA in UP.
detail.typicalUse: Any project needing environmental clearance — this is the actual filing system, not the secretariat's office contact.
quirks: SEIAA UP itself has no dedicated public website — all case processing runs through the national PARIVESH portal; don't waste time searching for a UP-specific SEIAA site

links.title: UPPCB — UP Pollution Control Board
links.note: State pollution-control consent (CTE/CTO) and monitoring.

detail.whatItGives: Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) application processes, plus pollution monitoring data.
detail.typicalUse: Pointing an investor to CTE/CTO application requirements.
quirks: Multiple lookalike/legacy domains exist for UPPCB (uppcb.com, uppcbims.co.in, uppcb-org.com) — this .up.gov.in address is the government-confirmed one; verify before trusting an alternate domain

An automated check hit a redirect to an internal error page (frmHttpErrorPage.aspx), the same pattern seen on GNIDA — likely anti-automation behavior on NIC-hosted UP sites rather than actual downtime; confirm manually in a browser

links.title: UPSIDA — Present Rates
links.note: Current per-sqm allotment rates across UPSIDA industrial areas.

detail.whatItGives: The authoritative current rate table by industrial area — distinct from PropertyHub's per-plot indicative pricing.
detail.typicalUse: Quoting the official current rate for an industrial area, not just an indicative plot price.
quirks: A staging-domain copy of this page (stagingupsida.com) surfaces in search results — always use the onlineupsida.com production URL, never the staging one

links.title: IGRSUP — Circle Rates (Stamp & Registration)
links.note: Official circle-rate lookup for stamp duty/valuation across UP.

detail.owner: Stamp & Registration Department, Govt. of UP
detail.whatItGives: District/tehsil/locality-level circle rates used for stamp duty and property valuation — the field a plain-text search for 'circle rate' should surface.
detail.typicalUse: Estimating stamp duty or minimum registration value for a land transaction.

links.title: UPSIDA Operating Manual
links.note: UPSIDA's internal operating procedures, publicly posted.

detail.whatItGives: The procedural rulebook UPSIDA staff themselves operate under — allotment process, transfer rules, penalty clauses.
detail.typicalUse: Settling a procedural dispute or question by citing UPSIDA's own manual rather than informal practice.
quirks: publishedDate left blank deliberately — the filename says '2023' but that isn't a confirmed publication date, so it isn't asserted here; source it from the document itself if it's needed

links.title: Uttar Pradesh Revenue Code, 2006
links.note: The consolidated state revenue/land law — 39 prior laws merged into one code.
links.issuingAuthority: Govt. of UP (U.P. Act No. 8 of 2012)

detail.owner: Govt. of UP — hosted on the central India Code repository
detail.whatItGives: The full statutory text governing land classification, revenue records, mutation, and related land-law questions across UP.
detail.typicalUse: Citing statutory basis for a land-classification or revenue-record question.
quirks: Complicated date history — drafted as a 2006 bill, but only received presidential assent on 29 Nov 2012 as U.P. Act No. 8 of 2012, published in the UP Gazette on 12 Dec 2012 (the date used here). Different sections then commenced on different notified dates — e.g. several core sections commenced only from 18 Dec 2015. Do not cite '2006' as the enactment date; verify which sections are in force for the specific provision you're citing.

links.title: UP RERA — Real Estate Regulatory Authority
links.note: Registered-project and promoter lookup — due diligence on any developer counterparty.

detail.owner: Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority (under the RERA Act, 2016)
detail.whatItGives: Searchable register of real estate projects and promoters/agents in UP, with registration status and complaint history — the public record for checking whether a developer and their project are actually registered and in good standing.
detail.typicalUse: Due diligence on a private developer counterparty — relevant to business park, plug-and-play shed, and private-township proposals where a developer partner is involved.
quirks: Registration lookups are served from a separate uprera.azurewebsites.net application — the domain change mid-journey is expected, not a phishing redirect
Covers real estate promoters, not industrial allottees — a unit taking a UPSIDA plot will not appear here

links.title: Invest UP — Official Site
links.note: Main Invest UP site — sector pages, news, and policy index.

detail.whatItGives: Sector overviews, news and events, and links into the broader policy index.
detail.typicalUse: Starting point for external-facing sector information to share with an investor.

links.title: Invest UP — Policies & Government Orders Index
links.note: The master list of every current UP industrial policy and GO — start here if a specific policy isn't yet in this index.

detail.whatItGives: A live, continuously-updated index of all state industrial policies and government orders — the fallback source when a specific policy entry here is missing or outdated.
detail.typicalUse: Checking whether a newer policy or amendment exists that this index hasn't caught up to yet.
quirks: This is a live index page, not a single dated document — that's why it lives here in Invest UP rather than in the sortable Policies table, which expects per-document dates

links.title: Invest UP — Udyami Mitra
links.note: District-level investor facilitation officers — who to contact on the ground.

detail.whatItGives: The Udyami Mitra scheme roster — professionally qualified facilitators assigned per district/region to bridge investors and government departments.
detail.typicalUse: Finding the named facilitation contact for a specific district when an investor needs boots-on-the-ground help.
quirks: Scheme launched 2023 as 'Mukhya Mantri Udyami Mitra' — roster/contacts may turn over; treat named contacts as more perishable than the rest of this index
